NASB.1: Then God said to Jacob, 'Arise, go up to Bethel and live there, and make an altar there to God, who appeared to you when you fled from your brother Esau.'
NASB.2: So Jacob said to his household and to all who were with him, 'Put away the foreign gods which are among you, and purify yourselves and change your garments;
NASB.3: and let us arise and go up to Bethel, and I will make an altar there to God, who answered me in the day of my distress and has been with me wherever I have gone.'
NASB.4: So they gave to Jacob all the foreign gods which they had and the rings which were in their ears, and Jacob hid them under the oak which was near Shechem.
NASB.5: As they journeyed, there was a great terror upon the cities which were around them, and they did not pursue the sons of Jacob.
NASB.6: So Jacob came to Luz (that is, Bethel), which is in the land of Canaan, he and all the people who were with him.
NASB.7: He built an altar there, and called the place El-bethel, because there God had revealed Himself to him when he fled from his brother.
NASB.8: Now Deborah, Rebekah's nurse, died, and she was buried below Bethel under the oak; it was named Allon-bacuth.
NASB.9: Then God appeared to Jacob again when he came from Paddan-aram, and He blessed him.
NASB.10: God said to him, 'Your name is Jacob; You shall no longer be called Jacob, But Israel shall be your name.' Thus He called him Israel.
NASB.11: God also said to him, 'I am God Almighty; Be fruitful and multiply; A nation and a company of nations shall come from you, And kings shall come forth from you.
NASB.12: 'The land which I gave to Abraham and Isaac, I will give it to you, And I will give the land to your descendants after you.'
NASB.13: Then God went up from him in the place where He had spoken with him.
NASB.14: Jacob set up a pillar in the place where He had spoken with him, a pillar of stone, and he poured out a drink offering on it; he also poured oil on it.
NASB.15: So Jacob named the place where God had spoken with him, Bethel.
NASB.16: Then they journeyed from Bethel; and when there was still some distance to go to Ephrath, Rachel began to give birth and she suffered severe labor.
NASB.17: When she was in severe labor the midwife said to her, 'Do not fear, for now you have another son.'
NASB.18: It came about as her soul was departing (for she died), that she named him Ben-oni; but his father called him Benjamin.
NASB.19: So Rachel died and was buried on the way to Ephrath (that is, Bethlehem).
NASB.20: Jacob set up a pillar over her grave; that is the pillar of Rachel's grave to this day.
NASB.21: Then Israel journeyed on and pitched his tent beyond the tower of Eder.
NASB.22: It came about while Israel was dwelling in that land, that Reuben went and lay with Bilhah his father's concubine, and Israel heard [of it]. Now there were twelve sons of Jacob--
NASB.23: the sons of Leah: Reuben, Jacob's firstborn, then Simeon and Levi and Judah and Issachar and Zebulun;
NASB.24: the sons of Rachel: Joseph and Benjamin;
NASB.25: and the sons of Bilhah, Rachel's maid: Dan and Naphtali;
NASB.26: and the sons of Zilpah, Leah's maid: Gad and Asher. These are the sons of Jacob who were born to him in Paddan-aram.
NASB.27: Jacob came to his father Isaac at Mamre of Kiriath-arba (that is, Hebron), where Abraham and Isaac had sojourned.
NASB.28: Now the days of Isaac were one hundred and eighty years.
NASB.29: Isaac breathed his last and died and was gathered to his people, an old man of ripe age; and his sons Esau and Jacob buried him.

ESV.1: God said to Jacob, “Arise, go up to Bethel and dwell there. Make an altar there to the God who appeared to you when you fled from your brother Esau.”
ESV.2: So Jacob said to his household and to all who were with him, “Put away the foreign gods that are among you and purify yourselves and change your garments.
ESV.3: Then let us arise and go up to Bethel, so that I may make there an altar to the God who answers me in the day of my distress and has been with me wherever I have gone.”
ESV.4: So they gave to Jacob all the foreign gods that they had, and the rings that were in their ears. Jacob hid them under the terebinth tree that was near Shechem.
ESV.5: And as they journeyed, a terror from God fell upon the cities that were around them, so that they did not pursue the sons of Jacob.
ESV.6: And Jacob came to Luz (that is, Bethel), which is in the land of Canaan, he and all the people who were with him,
ESV.7: and there he built an altar and called the place El-bethel,  because there God had revealed himself to him when he fled from his brother.
ESV.8: And Deborah, Rebekah's nurse, died, and she was buried under an oak below Bethel. So he called its name Allon-bacuth.
ESV.9: God appeared  to Jacob again, when he came from Paddan-aram, and blessed him.
ESV.10: And God said to him, “Your name is Jacob; no longer shall your name be called Jacob, but Israel shall be your name.” So he called his name Israel.
ESV.11: And God said to him, “I am God Almighty:  be fruitful and multiply. A nation and a company of nations shall come from you, and kings shall come from your own body.
ESV.12: The land that I gave to Abraham and Isaac I will give to you, and I will give the land to your offspring after you.”
ESV.13: Then God went up from him in the place where he had spoken with him.
ESV.14: And Jacob set up a pillar in the place where he had spoken with him, a pillar of stone. He poured out a drink offering on it and poured oil on it.
ESV.15: So Jacob called the name of the place where God had spoken with him Bethel.
ESV.16: Then they journeyed from Bethel. When they were still some distance  from Ephrath, Rachel went into labor, and she had hard labor.
ESV.17: And when her labor was at its hardest, the midwife said to her, “Do not fear, for you have another son.”
ESV.18: And as her soul was departing (for she was dying), she called his name Ben-oni;  but his father called him Benjamin.
ESV.19: So Rachel died, and she was buried on the way to Ephrath (that is, Bethlehem),
ESV.20: and Jacob set up a pillar over her tomb. It is the pillar of Rachel's tomb, which is there to this day.
ESV.21: Israel journeyed on and pitched his tent beyond the tower of Eder.
ESV.22: While Israel lived in that land, Reuben went and lay with Bilhah his father's concubine. And Israel heard of it. Now the sons of Jacob were twelve.
ESV.23: The sons of Leah: Reuben (Jacob's firstborn), Simeon, Levi, Judah, Issachar, and Zebulun.
ESV.24: The sons of Rachel: Joseph and Benjamin.
ESV.25: The sons of Bilhah, Rachel's servant: Dan and Naphtali.
ESV.26: The sons of Zilpah, Leah's servant: Gad and Asher. These were the sons of Jacob who were born to him in Paddan-aram.
ESV.27: And Jacob came to his father Isaac at Mamre, or Kiriath-arba (that is, Hebron), where Abraham and Isaac had sojourned.
ESV.28: Now the days of Isaac were 180 years.
ESV.29: And Isaac breathed his last, and he died and was gathered to his people, old and full of days. And his sons Esau and Jacob buried him.

NLT.1: Then God said to Jacob, “Get ready and move to Bethel and settle there. Build an altar there to the God who appeared to you when you fled from your brother, Esau.”
NLT.2: So Jacob told everyone in his household, “Get rid of all your pagan idols, purify yourselves, and put on clean clothing.
NLT.3: We are now going to Bethel, where I will build an altar to the God who answered my prayers when I was in distress. He has been with me wherever I have gone.”
NLT.4: So they gave Jacob all their pagan idols and earrings, and he buried them under the great tree near Shechem.
NLT.5: As they set out, a terror from God spread over the people in all the towns of that area, so no one attacked Jacob’s family.
NLT.6: Eventually, Jacob and his household arrived at Luz (also called Bethel) in Canaan.
NLT.7: Jacob built an altar there and named the place El-bethel (which means “God of Bethel”), because God had appeared to him there when he was fleeing from his brother, Esau.
NLT.8: Soon after this, Rebekah’s old nurse, Deborah, died. She was buried beneath the oak tree in the valley below Bethel. Ever since, the tree has been called Allon-bacuth (which means “oak of weeping”).
NLT.9: Now that Jacob had returned from Paddan-aram, God appeared to him again at Bethel. God blessed him,
NLT.10: saying, “Your name is Jacob, but you will not be called Jacob any longer. From now on your name will be Israel.” So God renamed him Israel.
NLT.11: Then God said, “I am El-Shaddai — ‘God Almighty.’ Be fruitful and multiply. You will become a great nation, even many nations. Kings will be among your descendants!
NLT.12: And I will give you the land I once gave to Abraham and Isaac. Yes, I will give it to you and your descendants after you.”
NLT.13: Then God went up from the place where he had spoken to Jacob.
NLT.14: Jacob set up a stone pillar to mark the place where God had spoken to him. Then he poured wine over it as an offering to God and anointed the pillar with olive oil.
NLT.15: And Jacob named the place Bethel (which means “house of God”), because God had spoken to him there.
NLT.16: Leaving Bethel, Jacob and his clan moved on toward Ephrath. But Rachel went into labor while they were still some distance away. Her labor pains were intense.
NLT.17: After a very hard delivery, the midwife finally exclaimed, “Don’t be afraid — you have another son!”
NLT.18: Rachel was about to die, but with her last breath she named the baby Ben-oni (which means “son of my sorrow”). The baby’s father, however, called him Benjamin (which means “son of my right hand”).
NLT.19: So Rachel died and was buried on the way to Ephrath (that is, Bethlehem).
NLT.20: Jacob set up a stone monument over Rachel’s grave, and it can be seen there to this day.
NLT.21: Then Jacob traveled on and camped beyond Migdal-eder.
NLT.22: While he was living there, Reuben had intercourse with Bilhah, his father’s concubine, and Jacob soon heard about it. These are the names of the twelve sons of Jacob:
NLT.23: The sons of Leah were Reuben (Jacob’s oldest son), Simeon, Levi, Judah, Issachar, and Zebulun.
NLT.24: The sons of Rachel were Joseph and Benjamin.
NLT.25: The sons of Bilhah, Rachel’s servant, were Dan and Naphtali.
NLT.26: The sons of Zilpah, Leah’s servant, were Gad and Asher. These are the names of the sons who were born to Jacob at Paddan-aram.
NLT.27: So Jacob returned to his father, Isaac, in Mamre, which is near Kiriath-arba (now called Hebron), where Abraham and Isaac had both lived as foreigners.
NLT.29: Then he breathed his last and died at a ripe old age, joining his ancestors in death. And his sons, Esau and Jacob, buried him.

CSB17.1: God said to Jacob, “Get up! Go to Bethel and settle there. <sup>ⓒ</sup> Build an altar there to the God who appeared to you when you fled from your brother Esau.” <sup>ⓓ</sup>
CSB17.2: So Jacob said to his family and all who were with him, “Get rid of the foreign gods that are among you. <sup>ⓔ</sup> Purify yourselves and change your clothes. <sup>ⓕ</sup>
CSB17.3: We must get up and go to Bethel. I will build an altar there to the God who answered me in my day of distress. <sup>ⓖ</sup> He has been with me everywhere I have gone.” <sup>ⓗ</sup>
CSB17.4: Then they gave Jacob all their foreign gods and their earrings, and Jacob hid them under the oak near Shechem.
CSB17.5: When they set out, a terror from God came over the cities around them, and they did not pursue Jacob’s sons. <sup>ⓘ</sup>
CSB17.6: So Jacob and all who were with him came to Luz (that is, Bethel <sup>ⓙ</sup>) in the land of Canaan.
CSB17.7: Jacob built an altar there and called the place El-bethel <sup>[1]</sup> because it was there that God had revealed himself to him when he was fleeing from his brother.
CSB17.8: Deborah, the one who had nursed and raised Rebekah, <sup>[2]</sup> <sup>ⓚ</sup> died and was buried under the oak south of Bethel. So Jacob named it Allon-bacuth. <sup>[3]</sup>
CSB17.9: God appeared to Jacob again after he returned from Paddan-aram, and he blessed him.
CSB17.10: God said to him, “Your name is Jacob; you will no longer be named Jacob, but your name will be Israel.” <sup>ⓛ</sup> So he named him Israel.
CSB17.11: God also said to him, “I am God Almighty. <sup>ⓜ</sup> Be fruitful and multiply. <sup>ⓝ</sup> A nation, indeed an assembly of nations, will come from you, <sup>ⓐ</sup> and kings will descend from you. <sup>[4]</sup> <sup>ⓑ</sup>
CSB17.12: I will give to you the land that I gave to Abraham and Isaac. <sup>ⓒ</sup> And I will give the land to your future descendants.”
CSB17.13: Then God withdrew <sup>[5]</sup> <sup>ⓓ</sup> from him at the place where he had spoken to him.
CSB17.14: Jacob set up a marker at the place where he had spoken to him — a stone marker. He poured a drink offering on it and anointed it with oil. <sup>ⓔ</sup>
CSB17.15: Jacob named the place where God had spoken with him Bethel.
CSB17.16: They set out from Bethel. When they were still some distance from Ephrath, Rachel began to give birth, and her labor was difficult.
CSB17.17: During her difficult labor, the midwife said to her, “Don’t be afraid, for you have another son.” <sup>ⓕ</sup>
CSB17.18: With her last breath — for she was dying — she named him Ben-oni, <sup>[6]</sup> but his father called him Benjamin. <sup>[7]</sup>
CSB17.19: So Rachel died and was buried on the way to Ephrath (that is, Bethlehem <sup>ⓖ</sup>).
CSB17.20: Jacob set up a marker on her grave; it is the marker at Rachel’s grave still today.
CSB17.21: Israel set out again and pitched his tent beyond the Tower of Eder. <sup>[8]</sup>
CSB17.22: While Israel was living in that region, Reuben went in and slept with his father’s concubine Bilhah, and Israel heard about it. <sup>ⓗ</sup> Jacob had twelve sons: <sup>ⓘ</sup>
CSB17.23: Leah’s sons were Reuben (Jacob’s firstborn), Simeon, Levi, Judah, Issachar, and Zebulun.
CSB17.24: Rachel’s sons were Joseph and Benjamin.
CSB17.25: The sons of Rachel’s slave Bilhah were Dan and Naphtali.
CSB17.26:
The sons of Leah’s slave Zilpah were Gad and Asher.
These are the sons of Jacob, who were born to him in Paddan-aram.
CSB17.27: Jacob came to his father Isaac at Mamre <sup>ⓙ</sup> in Kiriath-arba (that is, Hebron <sup>ⓚ</sup>), where Abraham and Isaac had stayed.
CSB17.29: He took his last breath and died, and was gathered to his people, <sup>ⓛ</sup> old and full of days. His sons Esau and Jacob buried him.

AMP.1: Then God said to Jacob, "Go up to Bethel and live there, and make an altar there to God, who appeared to you [in a distinct manifestation] when you fled [years ago] from Esau your brother."
AMP.2: Then Jacob said to his household and to all who were with him, "Get rid of the [idols and images of] foreign gods that are among you, and ceremonially purify yourselves and change [into fresh] clothes;
AMP.3: then let us get up and go up to Bethel, and I will make an altar there to God, who answered me in the day of my distress and has been with me wherever I have gone."
AMP.4: So they gave Jacob all the [idols and images of the] foreign gods they had and the rings which were in their ears [worn as charms against evil], and Jacob buried them under the oak tree near Shechem.
AMP.5: As they journeyed, there was a great [supernatural] terror [sent from God] on the cities around them, and [for that reason] the Canaanites did not pursue the sons of Jacob.
AMP.6: So Jacob came to Luz (that is, Bethel), which is in the land of Canaan, he and all the people who were with him.
AMP.7: There he built an altar [to worship the LORD], and called the place El-bethel (God of the House of God), because there God had revealed Himself to him when he escaped from his brother.
AMP.8: Now Deborah, [who once was] Rebekah's nurse, died and was buried below Bethel under the oak; and the name of it was called Allon-bacuth (Oak of Weeping).
AMP.9: Then God [in a visible manifestation] appeared to Jacob again when he came out of Paddan-aram, and declared a blessing on him.
AMP.10:
Again God said to him,
"Your name is Jacob;
You shall no longer be called Jacob,
But Israel shall be your name."
So he was called Israel.
AMP.11:
And God said to him,
"I am God Almighty.
Be fruitful and multiply;
A nation and a company of nations shall come from you,
And kings shall be born of your loins.
AMP.12:
"The land which I gave Abraham and Isaac
I will give to you,
and to your descendants after you I will give the land."
AMP.13: Then God ascended from Jacob in the place where He had spoken with him.
AMP.14: Jacob set up a pillar (memorial, monument) in the place where he had talked with God, a pillar of stone, and he poured a drink offering [of wine] on it; he also poured oil on it [to declare it sacred for God's purpose].
AMP.15: So Jacob named the place where God had spoken with him, Bethel (the House of God).
AMP.16: Then they journeyed from Bethel; and when there was still some distance to go to Ephrath (Bethlehem), Rachel began to give birth and had difficulty and suffered severely.
AMP.17: When she was in hard labor the midwife said to her, "Do not be afraid; you now have another son."
AMP.18: And as her soul was departing, (for she died), she named him Ben-oni (son of my sorrow); but his father called him Benjamin ( son of the right hand).
AMP.19: So Rachel died and was buried on the way to Ephrath (that is, Bethlehem).
AMP.20: Jacob set a pillar (memorial, monument) on her grave; that is the pillar of Rachel's grave to this day.
AMP.21: Then Israel (Jacob) journeyed on and pitched his tent on the other side of the tower of Eder [the lookout point used by shepherds].
AMP.22:
While Israel was living in that land, Reuben [his eldest son] went and lay with Bilhah his father's concubine, and Israel heard about it.
Now Jacob had twelve sons—
AMP.23: The sons of Leah: Reuben, Jacob's firstborn, then Simeon, Levi, Judah, Issachar, and Zebulun;
AMP.24: and the sons of Rachel: Joseph and Benjamin;
AMP.25: and the sons of Bilhah, Rachel's maid: Dan and Naphtali;
AMP.26: and the sons of Zilpah, Leah's maid: Gad and Asher. These are the sons of Jacob born to him in Paddan-aram.
AMP.27: Jacob came to Isaac his father at Mamre of Kiriath-arba (that is, Hebron), where Abraham and Isaac had lived temporarily.
AMP.28: Now the days of Isaac were a hundred and eighty years.
AMP.29: Isaac's spirit departed and he died and was gathered to his people [who had preceded him in death], an old man full of days (satisfied, fulfilled); his sons Esau and Jacob buried him [in the cave of Machpelah with his parents Abraham and Sarah].
